findings.description: The requirement bounds only the interval between consecutive services while integrity checks run. It does not bound the interval from watchdog activation to the first service or from the last service to the end of start-up; it can also be satisfied without two services. SYS-SUP-015 requires prevention of an independent watchdog reset throughout fault-free start-up.
findings.requested_change: Specify the software obligation that prevents an independent watchdog reset throughout fault-free start-up, including the first and last service intervals.

findings.description: The requirement constrains each window-watchdog refresh but does not require a refresh before the window expires. An implementation making no refresh satisfies the statement even if an enabled watchdog resets during fault-free start-up, contrary to SYS-SUP-015.
findings.requested_change: Specify the software obligation that prevents a window-watchdog reset throughout fault-free start-up, including refresh availability when the watchdog is enabled.

findings.description: The requirement assigns the supervisor software responsibility for holding the outputs low from any reset, including the interval before software configures the pins. CON-SUP-132 assigns the low level during that interval to external pull-down resistors, while the pins are inputs.
findings.requested_change: State the software-controlled portion of the low-output obligation and identify the external pull-down behavior as a hardware dependency.

findings.description: The requirement combines independently verifiable mappings for nine fault codes and multiple entity values. A report can use the correct mapping for one fault class and an incorrect mapping for another.
findings.requested_change: Split the mappings into independently judgeable requirements or reference a controlled mapping table with separately verifiable entries.

findings.description: Retention of the safe-state latch, per-code detection counts and fault history are independently verifiable obligations: any one can be retained across resets while another is lost.
findings.requested_change: Separate the retention obligations for the latch, detection counts and fault history.
